found.why: 'You are One' is said at Shabbat Minchah because the Holy One, the Torah and Israel are then one, joined to 'מנוחת שלום ושלוה השקט ובטח'. This parallels Rav Tzadok's reading of 'Atah Echad' as the union of Hashem and Israel, though it stresses love among Israel.

footnotes.text:
**Likutei Halakhot, Orach Chaim, Hil. Birchot HaShachar 5:26** (Chassidus) — R. Nosson explains that at Shabbat Minchah one rises to the supernal will, where the Holy One, the Torah and Israel are one, and so we say "You are One"; he joins this to "a rest of peace, tranquility, quiet and security." Like Rav Tzadok, he reads "Atah Echad" as the union of Hashem with Israel at Minchah.
וְעַל-כֵּן אוֹמְרִים בְּמִנְחָה בְּשַׁבָּת 'אַתָּה אֶחָד וְשִׁמְךָ אֶחָד וּמִי כְּעַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל גּוֹי אֶחָד בָּאָרֶץ'

footnotes.ref: Sha'arei Orah, Third and Fourth Gates, Seventh and Eight Sefirah 63-67
footnotes.text:
**Sha'arei Orah (R. Yosef Gikatilla), Gates 3–4** (Kabbalah) — Children, life and sustenance hang on the "supernal Mazal" in Keter, above the court of merit. Channah prayed "על ה'", above the Name Havayah, up to Ehyeh, and "השלך על ה' יהבך" works the same way. This is the chain Rav Tzadok draws from Moed Katan 28a and Zohar III 79b: mazal is Atika, above the Name.
המושכת הבנים ממזל כתר שהוא המזל העליון בסוד יג מידות רחמים הקבועים בכתר כי מאותו המזל בנים חיים ומזונות תלוים

**Zohar Chadash, Bereishis (Midrash HaNe'elam)** (Kabbalah) — Aravot holds the treasuries of rain and of good life and "many treasuries." It asks how this fits the teaching that there is only one otzar, and answers that there are two storehouses of souls. Rav Tzadok deals with the same tension, many ganzim against one otzar, but resolves it differently: the otzar is the vessel that holds the treasures.
ובערבות יש גנזים הרבה וגנזי הנשמות שם והא אמר רבי בא שאוצר אחד הוא והכא תנינן גנזים

**Degel Machaneh Ephraim, Vayigash** (Chassidus) — The Holy One has three treasuries: fear of Heaven, Shabbat ("a precious gift in My treasure-house") and Israel as His segulah. Against "He has nothing but a storehouse of fear of Heaven," all three are included in the otzar of fear of Heaven, Shabbat through "one who fears the Shabbat." This is the same resolution as Rav Tzadok's: Shabbat sits within the storehouse of fear.
י"ל דבאמת כל הג' אוצרות הם אוצר של יראת שמים ונכללו בו כי שבת היינו ע"ד ירא שבת

**Torah Ohr, Vayeshev** (Chassidus) — The Alter Rebbe explains the "otzar of fear of Heaven" as the higher fear, a receiving vessel in which supernal Chochmah rests and is revealed. This is close to Rav Tzadok's point that an otzar is a vessel that holds His treasures.
וכן בדברי רז"ל אוצר של יראת שמים שהיא בחי' יראה עילאה יראה בשת בבחי' בטול הוא כלי קבול לחכמה עילאה

**Noam Elimelech, Terumah** (Chassidus) — On "children, life and sustenance depend on Mazal," R. Elimelech says that weekdays are "merit" but holy Shabbat is "Mazal" (= 78, three Havayahs), corresponding to the three Shabbat meals. Through them the tzaddik draws down life, children and sustenance, which is Rav Tzadok's conclusion that the three treasuries hanging on Atika are merited in the three meals.
והם כנגד שלש סעודות של שבת קודש, וע"י הצדיק ממשיך את השלש הנ"ל
